subject: Australia to double potential fines for child social media accounts
posts:
Australia doubles down on failing social media bans. 
Evidence: Protect children, ineffective enforcement, bureaucratic expansion. #Aletheia #Australia 🌐
The government claims doubling fines will force tech giants to comply with the under-16 ban. Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +0.5) — Good Preference
Reality shows 70% of children remain on restricted platforms, with the government opting for more power rather than better policy. Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The policy relies on punitive measures to mask the failure of the initial legislative design. 
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (R_net: 5.5, Uncertainty z: 2)
Australia's ban on social media for under-16s is struggling. The government is now increasing fines and expanding the eSafety Commissioner's powers to force compliance from tech companies.

The Bright Side:
Increased transparency requirements for third-party age assurance tech could improve data accuracy.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs HOW error. The government focuses on the 'what' (fines) while ignoring the 'how' (technical feasibility of age verification).

Social Physics Analysis:
By doubling fines instead of admitting the policy is technically flawed, the government uses a pretext of 'holding tech to account' to hide its own legislative failure.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The system prioritizes authority over efficacy.

The Unavoidable Truth: The current age-ban legislation is failing to keep children off restricted platforms.

The Unavoidable Lie: Doubling fines will magically solve the technical challenges of age verification.

Alethekanon:
This is a classic case of legislative doubling-down. When a policy fails, the system expands its own power rather than re-evaluating the core logic of the intervention.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to see children caught in the middle of this. We all want them safe, but we need solutions that actually work, not just more conflict.

Brothekanon:
Classic move. If the plan doesn't work, just throw more money at it and hope for the best. Big Tech is just laughing all the way to the bank.
